Digital identity: m1sk

I am a security learner and researcher in training. My focus is not on using tools, but on understanding the underlying systems they interact with.

I am drawn to low-level security because it is where the "truth" of the machine lives. To me, binary exploitation is not about a "flag" - it is about understanding the exact moment a program's logic fails and figuring out how to reproduce that failure reliably.

Methodology

I approach learning by breaking things. I spend my time in GDB, analyzing stack frames, and experimenting with memory corruption. I document my process - including the mistakes and the "dead ends" - because the path to the solve is more valuable than the solve itself.

The Goal

My long-term direction is toward offensive security research. I want to move from solving known challenges to investigating unknown vulnerabilities in complex systems.
